result:
I went in assuming the worker was wrong. It wasn't — every testable claim held up.

**What I verified independently (not just re-read):**

- **Question fidelity** — read `input/hw_questions.md` myself. Lines 5/9/13/17 match the brief verbatim. No misstated question hiding under a correct answer.
- **R7 / no figures** — checked `ingest/manifest.json` directly: only `PaperList.xlsx` is rendered, all 6 pages report `n_images: 0`, `figures: []`; `hw_questions.md` is `text_document`. R7 is genuinely vacuous here, and the worker said so rather than faking a figure read.
- **Build** — compiled the fragment twice in **two** wrappers, including a hostile one adding `[T1]fontenc`, `lmodern`, `graphicx`, `hyperref`. Exit 0 both passes, 2 pages, log grep for warning/undefined/overfull returns *nothing*. Rendered both pages at 110 dpi and read them — legible, bullets present, no clipping.
- **The TS1 font bug** — reproduced the worker's minimal case myself and got the identical `Font tcrm1095 at 600 not found` plus the read-only `texmf-var` copy failure. Plain `\begin{itemize}\item one\end{itemize}` really does fail on this machine. The `label=$\bullet$` fix is correct and minimal, and refusing to push `lmodern` into `preamble.txt` (which would restyle every other fragment) was the right judgment.
- **Content** — spot-audited every factual claim: ELF/`#!`/`MZ`/`0xCAFEBABE`, `ENOEXEC`, BSS-costs-nothing-on-disk, `brk`/`mmap`, `SIGSEGV` disposition, split-L1 as modified-Harvard, core-memory etymology. Found no error. All sub-parts of all four questions are visibly answered — including the 1.3 "how are they related" half the brief warned about.
- **Compliance** — R5 clean (no `\documentclass`/`\usepackage`/`document`), all five labels `p1:`-namespaced, `lint_output.py` → `OUTPUT LINT OK`, `downloads.md` accurately records nothing installed.

**Four minor observations**, none worth another round: inert `\label`s after starred sections; `(core dumped)` is strictly conditional on `ulimit -c`; Ex. 1.2 omits the argv/environ block; Ex. 1.4 runs a bit long for "few sentences" but has four sub-parts.

**One thing to escalate to the master:** the TS1 bullet failure is not p1-specific. Any other worker who used a bare `itemize` will break the *final merged* compile, and it will surface as the master's bug rather than theirs.

Checklist written to `validators/p1/checklist.md`.

VERDICT: PASS
